name: obengineer
description: Instrumentation architecture workflows for Codex: analyze a target, write the one customer document, lay the wiki the agents retrieve from, and configure the tenant as Terraform.

interface.shortDescription: Instrumentation contracts for Splunk Observability Cloud, Enterprise, and ThousandEyes.
interface.longDescription:
obengineer turns an application into an instrumentation contract a team can implement, CI can enforce, and a TAM can configure.

It scans the target for what is actually there — which agent initialises and when, what else is collecting the same events, where the account and bus boundaries fall — then writes one customer document: observed architecture, critical findings with remediation, cross-cutting attributes and W3C Baggage propagation, the business-transaction and workflow registry, Collector configuration, dashboards, detectors with thresholds, objectives in the customer's voice, and the attribute dictionary. That document ships as Markdown and as a Word document rendered from the same source, so the two cannot disagree.

Underneath it, the agents work from a wiki — one note per subject under wiki/<Customer>/<app>/ — which is what makes a repeat run a delta rather than a rewrite, and a CI pipeline possible at all.

How to get started:
1. Install the obengineer plugin.
2. Review and trust the SessionStart hook when Codex prompts you.
3. Try: collect the inputs with $engagement-intake, analyze a target and write the document with $instrumentation-analyze, lay the agent wiki with $instrumentation-wiki, or emit Terraform with $observability-as-code.
defaultPrompt: Analyze this application and write the instrumentation document.
Build the agent wiki from the accepted analysis.
Render the document as a customer-review Word document.
